messages:
nora: RFC follow-up: RAM-only verifier with chunked artifact apply for air-gapped nodes. goal: avoid persistent signing keys on device, enable resumable installs, and provide a compact attestation receipt when the node reconnects.

sam: high-level sounds good. can you walk through power-loss recovery? thats the main customer ask.

nora: flow: (1) operator ships media with signed manifest + shard files, (2) on node a small verifier binary (loaded into RAM from media) validates manifest signatures, then streams shards into a staging area using sparse writes, validating each shard checksum, (3) once all shards verified we atomically switch active pointer and write a minimal activation marker that is cryptographically bound to ephemeral verifier key. if power-loss occurs before marker is durable, boot will ignore staged content. marker is tiny and the only persistent record.

jorge: question: where do we keep the trust anchors if we don't persist keys? media-supplied anchor bundle? what prevents an offline attacker from swapping the media?

nora: trust anchors are bundled with the media and are immutable for that release; operators should sign the whole media image with their offline key before shipping. additionally we include a manifest freshness counter + sequence number in anchors to detect replayed older media. if firmware root-of-trust exists, it should verify the bootloader too.

anya: operationally, how do we do phased rollouts / canaries if distribution is physical?

nora: manifest supports multiple candidates and an activation-policy field that only allows certain staged-ids if they carry an operator canary flag. local verifier enforces that policy. For fleet-level canaries you still need manual/physical staging sequencing or courier tagging.

sam: large model blobs may not fit disk when staged. any streaming/resume plan?

jorge: we propose content-addressed chunking: split big blobs into N 16MB+ chunks, store them as shards with a small index. verifier writes chunks to a sparse overlay and keeps a per-chunk applied bitmap + tombstone log so partial installs can resume. chunk manifests allow parallel apply and integrity checks.

nora: sample chunk index excerpt we discussed: ```
index:
  release: rlz-26-03
  shards:
    - name: model-v2.blob.chunks
      chunks: 764
      chunk_size: 16MB
      root_digest: sha256:fff..
    - name: runtime.patch
      chunks: 5
```

anya: telemetry/attestation on reconnect is sensitive. what does the receipt look like?

nora: verifier emits a tiny, signed receipt: {staged_id, result, applied_shard_roots, verifier_pub, proof_nonce}. Receipt is serialized compactly (protobuf-lite) and excludes runtime metadata. Control plane verifies the signature against the anchor bundle and checks sequence numbers. receipts are intentionally minimal to reduce exfil risk.

sam: what about rollback performance? customers want quick revert if new model regresses.

jorge: add a manifest flag "retain_previous: N" which keeps the previous N activations on disk (or their chunk indexes) to enable fast rollback. tradeoff: disk footprint and complexity. We should expose retention policy per-release in the manifest.

nora: also support a lightweight "fast-rollback" mode that only retains chunk indexes and dedup metadata, not full blobs, to allow on-disk rehydrate from artifact media if needed.

anya: security: physical compromise at courier could tamper media. mitigations?

nora: (1) operator offline-signs media; (2) anchors include operator-escrow cross-sigs; (3) make anchor changes highly visible in control-plane on first reconnect; (4) optional hardware root-of-trust check if device supports it. these reduce but don't eliminate risk.

sam: implementation tasks? rough list please.

nora: PoC deliverables: small Rust verifier binary, chunked apply library, overlayfs staging harness, compact receipt proto, integration tests for mid-apply power-loss and resume, and a simple control-plane verifier that accepts receipts. owners: @nora, @jorge.

ops-bot: action: create RFC doc + PoC ticket in eng-infra. assignees: nora, jorge. due: 2026-04-22.

jorge: one more UX note: manifest should have a human-readable courier tag section so operators can annotate physical shippings with expected content hashes to help on-site verification.

nora: good call. I'll include examples, threat model, sequence diagrams, and a proposed manifest schema in the RFC draft. sharing by EOD Monday for comments. :thumbsup:
